passages.basmala_hamdala.p01: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Allah's blessings and peace be on Muhammad, our master, and on his family and Companions.
passages.basmala_hamdala.p02: All praise is for Allah, Lord of all the worlds. Blessings and peace be on Muhammad, our master, the final Prophet and the leader of all the Messengers.
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.p01: The first thing required of the accountable person (mukallaf: someone sane and mature, and so bound by Islamic law) is to make sure that their faith (iman) is sound. After that, they must learn what they need in order to carry out their personal obligations (fard 'ayn: duties binding on every individual) correctly, for example the rulings on prayer, purification and fasting.
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.p02: They must also keep within the limits Allah has set, abide by what He commands and what He forbids, and turn to Allah, glorified is He, in repentance before He becomes displeased with them.
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.p03: Repentance (tawbah) has three conditions: remorse for what has passed; the intention never to return to a sin for as long as one lives; and, if one is in the middle of a sin, abandoning it at that very moment. It is not permissible to put off repentance, nor to say, "Not until Allah guides me." Talk like that is one of the marks of wretchedness, of being forsaken [by Allah], and of inner sight being blotted out.
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.p04: They must guard their tongue against indecency, wrongful talk and ugly words, and against swearing oaths by divorce [such as "If I do this, my wife is divorced"]; and against shouting at a fellow Muslim, belittling them, insulting them or frightening them without a right recognised by the Sacred Law (Shari'ah).
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.p05: They must keep their eyes from looking at what is forbidden. It is not permissible to give a Muslim a look that hurts them, unless that person is a fasiq (someone who openly persists in serious sin), in which case it is obligatory to keep away from them.
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.p06: They must protect all their limbs [from wrongdoing] as far as they are able. They must love for Allah's sake and dislike for His sake, be pleased for His sake and be angry for His sake. They must call others to what is right and forbid what is wrong.
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.p07: It is forbidden (haram) for them to lie, to backbite, to carry tales between people, to be arrogant or vain, to do good deeds so as to be seen or talked about, to envy, to bear hatred, [to regard oneself as superior to others, to disparage people by word or gesture (hamz and lamz), to indulge in idle frivolity,] or to make fun of others. Also forbidden are fornication and adultery (zina); looking at a woman one is neither married to nor closely related to (ajnabiyyah) and taking pleasure in her speech; consuming people's property without their willing consent; making a living out of intercession or out of religion; and putting off the prayer past its time.
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.p08: It is not permissible for them to befriend a fasiq or sit with one without necessity, nor to seek the approval of created beings at the cost of the Creator's displeasure. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says: "It is Allah and His Messenger whom they should rather please, if they are believers" (Qur'an 9:62). And the Prophet ﷺ said: "No created being may be obeyed in anything that disobeys the Creator."
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.p09: It is not permissible to do any act until one knows Allah's ruling on it, asking the scholars and following the example of those who hold to the Sunnah of [Muhammad] ﷺ: people who point the way to obeying Allah and warn people not to follow Satan.
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.p10: They should not be content for themselves with what satisfies the spiritually bankrupt, whose lives were wasted on things other than obeying Allah, exalted is He. How great their regret will be, and how long their weeping on the Day of Resurrection! Our plea to Allah is that He help us follow the Sunnah of Muhammad ﷺ, our Prophet, our intercessor and our master.
passages.tahara_purification.p01: Purification (taharah) is of two kinds: purification from ritual impurity (hadath: the state that calls for wudu or ghusl) and purification from physical filth (khabath). Neither is valid except with water that is pure and purifying (tahur). This means water that has kept its colour, taste and smell, unchanged by anything normally separate from it, such as oil, clarified butter or any kind of grease, animal dung, soap, grime and the like.
passages.tahara_purification.p02: There is no harm, however, in [a change caused by] earth, black mud, salty soil, baked brick and the like.
passages.najasa_impurity.p01: When the exact spot of an impurity (najasah: an impure substance) is known, one washes that spot; when the spot is uncertain, one washes the entire garment.
passages.najasa_impurity.p02: Someone who is unsure whether an impurity has touched [something] sprinkles it with water (nadh). If something touches them and they are unsure whether that thing is impure, they do not need to sprinkle anything.
passages.najasa_impurity.p03: Someone who remembers an impurity while praying must break off the prayer, unless they fear the prayer time will run out. Someone who prayed with it out of forgetfulness and remembered after the closing salam (saying "as-salamu 'alaykum" to end the prayer) repeats the prayer within its time.
passages.wudu_faraid_sunan.p01: [The obligatory acts (fard: required, so that wudu, the minor ablution, is invalid without them) are:] the intention (niyyah); washing the face; washing the arms, from the fingertips to the elbows [with the elbows themselves washed]; wiping the head; washing the feet as far as the ankles [with the ankle bones washed]; rubbing each part with the hand while washing (dalk); and continuity (fawr: doing it without a long break).
passages.wudu_faraid_sunan.p02: Its sunnahs (practices established by the Prophet ﷺ) are: washing the hands as far as the wrists before beginning; rinsing the mouth; drawing water into the nose; blowing it out; bringing the hands back over the head after wiping it; wiping the ears and taking fresh water for them; and keeping the obligatory acts in their proper order.
passages.wudu_faraid_sunan.p03: Someone who forgets one of the obligatory parts: if they remember soon afterwards, they do that part and everything that follows it; but after a long gap, they do that part alone and repeat any prayer they performed before doing it. Someone who left out a sunnah does it and does not repeat the prayer.
passages.wudu_faraid_sunan.p04: Someone who missed a small spot (lum'ah) washes that spot alone, with an intention; if they prayed before doing so, they repeat the prayer. Someone who remembers rinsing the mouth and nose only after starting on the face does not go back to them until they have finished their wudu.
passages.wudu_faraid_sunan.p05: Its meritorious acts (fada'il, singular fadilah: recommended acts that bring extra reward) are: saying "Bismillah"; using the tooth-stick (siwak); going beyond the first washing of the face and arms; starting the wipe of the head from the front; keeping the sunnahs in order; using little water on each part; and doing the right side before the left.
passages.wudu_faraid_sunan.p06: It is obligatory to work water between the fingers (takhlil), and recommended to do so between the toes. It is obligatory in wudu to work water through a beard that is thin, though not through a thick one; in ghusl, even a thick beard must have water worked through it.
passages.wudu_nullifiers.p01: The events (ahdath: things that break wudu by their very occurrence) are: urine, faeces, wind, madhy (pre-seminal fluid) and wady (a thick white fluid that may come out after urinating).
passages.wudu_nullifiers.p02: The causes (asbab: things that lead to wudu being broken) are: deep sleep, fainting, intoxication, insanity, kissing, touching a woman if one intended pleasure or felt it, and touching the penis with the inner palm or the inner side of the fingers.
passages.wudu_nullifiers.p03: Someone who is in doubt about whether something has broken their wudu must perform wudu, unless they suffer from obsessive doubts (waswasah), in which case nothing is required of them.
passages.wudu_nullifiers.p04: Madhy requires washing the whole penis, but not the testicles. Madhy is the fluid released during mild sexual arousal, brought on through thoughts, glances or something similar.
passages.acts_requiring_wudu.p01: Someone without wudu (the minor ablution) may not pray, perform tawaf (circling the Ka'bah), or touch a copy (mushaf) of the Mighty Qur'an, or its cover, whether by hand, with a stick or anything similar, except for a portion of it that one is studying from.
passages.acts_requiring_wudu.p02: Nor may they touch a board with Qur'an written on it (lawh) without wudu, except for a student using it to learn, or a teacher who is correcting it.
passages.acts_requiring_wudu.p03: A child is like an adult with regard to touching the Qur'an, and the sin falls on whoever hands it to them.
passages.acts_requiring_wudu.p04: Whoever prays without wudu on purpose is a disbeliever (kafir). We seek refuge in Allah.
passages.ghusl_causes.p01: [They are:] janabah (the state of major ritual impurity caused by sexual discharge or intercourse), menstruation (hayd) and postnatal bleeding (nifas).
passages.ghusl_causes.p02: Janabah is of two kinds. The first is the emission of semen with the usual pleasure, whether asleep or awake, through intercourse or otherwise. The second is the head of the penis fully entering the private part.
passages.ghusl_causes.p03: Someone who dreams they are having intercourse, but no semen comes out, owes nothing.
passages.ghusl_causes.p04: Someone who finds dry semen on their clothing and has no idea when it happened takes a ghusl and repeats the prayers they performed since the last time they slept in [that garment].
passages.ghusl_faraid_sunan.p01: [They are:] the intention at the start; continuity (fawr: without a long break); rubbing (dalk); and making the water reach the whole body.
passages.ghusl_faraid_sunan.p02: Its sunnahs (practices established by the Prophet ﷺ): washing the hands as far as the wrists, just as in wudu; rinsing the mouth; drawing water into the nose and blowing it out; and washing the ear canal (simakh), which is the opening that leads into the head. As for the outer ear, it is obligatory to wash both its outer and inner surfaces.
passages.ghusl_faraid_sunan.p03: Its meritorious acts (fada'il: recommended acts that bring extra reward): beginning by washing off any impurity, then washing the private part, with the intention made at that moment; then the parts washed in wudu, once each; then the upper body; washing the head three times; starting with the right side of the body; and using little water on each part.
passages.ghusl_faraid_sunan.p04: Someone who left a small spot or a whole limb unwashed in their ghusl hurries to wash it as soon as they remember, even a month later, and repeats any prayers performed before that. If they delay after remembering, their ghusl is void. If [the missed spot] was among the parts of wudu, and the washing done in a wudu reached it, that is enough.
passages.junub_prohibitions.p01: Someone in a state of janabah (major ritual impurity) may not enter a mosque, nor recite the Qur'an except a verse or so recited for protection or a similar purpose.
passages.junub_prohibitions.p02: A man who cannot use cold water may not approach his wife [for intercourse] before he has made ready the means [of heating water]; but a wet dream brings no blame on him.
passages.tayammum.p01: Tayammum (purification by wiping with clean earth) is performed [when water is unavailable or cannot be used] by a traveller whose journey is not for a sinful purpose, and by a sick person, for both obligatory and voluntary prayers.
passages.tayammum.p02: A healthy resident (someone not travelling) performs tayammum for obligatory prayers if they fear the prayer time will run out. It is not allowed for a healthy resident to use tayammum for a voluntary prayer, for Jumu'ah (the Friday prayer) or for a funeral prayer, unless that funeral prayer has become their own individual duty.
passages.tayammum.p03: Its obligatory acts (fard: required for validity): the intention; pure earth (sa'id); wiping the face; wiping the hands as far as the wrists; the first strike [of the hands] on the earth; continuity; that the prayer time has begun; and that the prayer follows it directly.
passages.tayammum.p04: Sa'id means soil, unbaked brick, stone, snow, watery mud and the like.
passages.tayammum.p05: Tayammum is not permitted on baked plaster, mats, wood, grass or similar things. A sick person is allowed to use a wall of stone or unbaked brick if they find no one to bring them anything else.
passages.tayammum.p06: Its sunnahs (practices established by the Prophet ﷺ): a second strike on the earth for the hands; wiping from the wrists to the elbows; and doing it in order.
passages.tayammum.p07: Its meritorious acts (fada'il: recommended acts that bring extra reward): saying "Bismillah"; doing the right side before the left; wiping the outer forearm before the inner; and starting from the front end of the limb before the back.
passages.tayammum.p08: Its nullifiers are the same as those of wudu. Two obligatory prayers may not be prayed with a single tayammum.
passages.tayammum.p09: Someone who performs tayammum for an obligatory prayer may afterwards pray voluntary prayers, touch the mushaf (a copy of the Qur'an), do tawaf and recite [the Qur'an], provided they intended this, it follows the prayer without a break, and the prayer time has not ended. A tayammum made for a voluntary prayer permits everything mentioned except an obligatory prayer.
passages.tayammum.p10: Someone who prays 'Isha with tayammum stands up for shaf' and witr (the even and odd night prayers) straight afterwards, without delay. Someone performing tayammum because of janabah must specifically intend that.
passages.hayd_menstruation.p01: Women [in this matter] are of three kinds: those menstruating for the first time (mubtada'ah), those with an established pattern (mu'tadah), and pregnant women.
passages.hayd_menstruation.p02: The longest that menstruation can last for a girl's first period is fifteen days. For a woman with an established pattern it is her usual length; if the bleeding continues beyond that, she adds three days, as long as the total does not exceed fifteen days.
passages.hayd_menstruation.p03: For a pregnant woman after three months [of pregnancy], it is fifteen days or thereabouts; after six months, twenty days or thereabouts.
passages.hayd_menstruation.p04: If the bleeding stops and starts, she adds up the days of bleeding until they reach her usual length.
passages.hayd_menstruation.p05: During menstruation a woman may not pray, fast, do tawaf, touch a mushaf (copy of the Qur'an) or go into a mosque. She must later make up the missed fasts, though not the prayers. She may recite [the Qur'an].
passages.hayd_menstruation.p06: Her husband may not have intercourse with her, nor enjoy the area between her navel and knees, until she has bathed with a ghusl (the full ritual bath).
passages.nifas_postnatal.p01: Postnatal bleeding (nifas) prohibits the same things as menstruation. It lasts at most sixty days. If the bleeding stops before that, even on the very day she gives birth, she takes a ghusl and prays.
passages.nifas_postnatal.p02: If the bleeding then comes back: if fifteen days or more separate the two, the second bleeding counts as menstruation; if not, it is counted with the first and completes the nifas.
passages.salah_times.p01: The preferred time (mukhtar) for Zuhr runs from the moment the sun passes its zenith until the end of the qamah [when an object's shadow equals its own height, not counting its shadow at noon]. The preferred time for 'Asr runs from the qamah until the sunlight turns yellow. The extended time (daruri: the period that follows the preferred time) for both lasts until sunset.
passages.salah_times.p02: The preferred time for Maghrib is just long enough to pray it after meeting its conditions. The preferred time for 'Isha runs from when the twilight (shafaq: the red glow after sunset) has vanished until a third of the night has passed. For both, the extended time lasts until dawn (fajr) breaks.
passages.salah_times.p03: The preferred time for Subh (the dawn prayer) runs from dawn until the light has fully spread (isfar); its extended time lasts until sunrise.
passages.salah_times.p04: Praying any of them after these times counts as a make-up (qada').
passages.salah_times.p05: Anyone who lets a prayer's time run out before praying it bears a grave sin, unless they forgot or were asleep.
passages.salah_times.p06: No voluntary prayer is to be prayed from the end of Subh until the sun is higher in the sky; from the end of 'Asr until Maghrib has been prayed; or after dawn breaks, except for a person's regular night devotions (wird) that they slept through. Nor is it to be prayed while the imam of Jumu'ah is seated on the pulpit, or after Jumu'ah until one leaves the mosque.
passages.salah_conditions.p01: The conditions of the prayer (shurut: things that must be in place for it to be valid) are: purity from ritual impurity (hadath); purity from physical filth (khabath) on one's body, clothes and the place where one prays; covering the 'awrah (the parts of the body that must be covered); facing the qiblah (the direction of the Ka'bah); refraining from speech; and refraining from excessive movement.
passages.salah_conditions.p02: A man's 'awrah is what lies between the navel and the knee. A woman's whole body is 'awrah except the face and hands.
passages.salah_conditions.p03: Praying in trousers alone is disliked (makruh: discouraged, though not sinful), unless something is worn over them.
passages.salah_conditions.p04: If someone's garment becomes impure and they cannot find another garment or water to wash it, or they have nothing else to wear while they wash it, [and they fear] the time will run out, they pray in it, impurity and all.
passages.salah_conditions.p05: It is not permissible to put off the prayer for lack of purification; whoever does so has disobeyed their Lord.
passages.salah_conditions.p06: Someone who cannot find anything to cover their 'awrah prays unclothed.
passages.salah_conditions.p07: Someone who got the qiblah wrong repeats the prayer within its time. Any repetition made within the time is a fadilah (a recommended act, not an obligation). Whatever leads to a prayer being repeated within its time does not lead to repeating a make-up prayer or a voluntary one.
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.p01: [The obligatory acts (fard: required, so that the prayer is invalid without them) are:] the intention for the particular prayer; the opening takbir (takbirat al-ihram: saying "Allahu akbar" to enter the prayer) and standing for it; the Fatihah (the opening chapter of the Qur'an) and standing for it; bowing (ruku') and rising from it; prostrating (sujud) on the forehead and rising from it; standing upright (i'tidal); stillness in each position (tuma'ninah); keeping the obligatory acts in order; the closing salam; and the sitting that goes with it.
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.p02: The condition of the intention: it must coincide with the opening takbir.
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.p03: Its sunnahs (practices established by the Prophet ﷺ): the iqamah (the second call, given just before the prayer begins); the surah after the Fatihah, and standing for it; reciting quietly where quiet recitation applies and aloud where loud recitation applies; saying "Sami'a Allahu liman hamidah" (Allah hears whoever praises Him); every takbir except the first; both tashahhuds (the testimony recited while sitting) and the sitting for them; reciting the Fatihah before the surah; the second and third salams for a follower; saying the obligatory salam aloud; and sending blessings (salawat) upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.p04: Also sunnah: prostrating on the nose, the palms, the knees and the ends of the toes; and a sutrah (a barrier placed in front of the person praying) for anyone not praying behind an imam. At minimum it should be as thick as a spear and a forearm's length in height, pure, firmly in place and not distracting.
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.p05: Its meritorious acts (fada'il: recommended acts that bring extra reward): raising the hands at the opening takbir up to ear level; the follower and the person praying alone saying "Rabbana wa laka al-hamd" (Our Lord, and to You belongs all praise); saying "Amin" after the Fatihah, for the person praying alone and for the follower, while the imam says it only when the recitation is silent; glorifying Allah (tasbih) in bowing; and making supplication (du'a) in prostration.
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.p06: Also: making the recitation long in Subh, with Zuhr a little shorter; short in 'Asr and Maghrib; and of medium length in 'Isha. And the first surah should come ahead of the second [in Qur'anic order] and be longer than it.
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.p07: Also: the known postures in bowing, prostration and sitting; reciting the qunut (a supplication made while standing) quietly, before bowing and after the surah, in the second rak'ah (cycle of prayer) of Subh, though it may also be said [after] bowing; supplication after the second tashahhud; making the second tashahhud longer than the first; turning to the right at the salam; and moving the forefinger in the tashahhud.
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.p08: It is disliked (makruh: discouraged, though not sinful) to turn [the head] in prayer, to close the eyes, or to say the basmalah ("Bismillah...") and the ta'awwudh ("A'udhu billah...") in an obligatory prayer; both are allowed in voluntary prayers.
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.p09: Also disliked: standing on one foot, unless one has been standing a long time; pressing the feet together; keeping a coin or anything else in the mouth, and likewise anything that distracts one, whether in a pocket, a sleeve or on the back; thinking about worldly matters; and anything that draws one's attention away from humility (khushu') in prayer.
passages.salah_khushu.p01: Prayer has a great light that makes the hearts of worshippers shine, and only those with khushu' (humble, attentive presence before Allah) attain it. So when you come to pray, free your heart from this world and all it holds, and busy yourself with being mindful of your Master, for whose sake you are praying. Hold firmly that prayer is humility and lowliness before Allah, glorified is He, through standing, bowing and prostrating, and that it is honouring and magnifying Him through takbir, tasbih and remembrance (dhikr).
passages.salah_khushu.p02: So guard your prayer, for it is the greatest of all acts of worship. Do not let Satan play with your heart and draw you away from the prayer, until your heart grows dark and you are deprived of the sweetness of the prayer's lights.
passages.salah_khushu.p03: Hold on to khushu' constantly in your prayer, for it is through khushu' that prayer keeps a person away from indecency and wrongdoing. Seek Allah's help, for He is the best one to turn to for help.
passages.salah_seven_states.p01: An obligatory prayer can be performed in seven positions, taken in a fixed order: four of them obligatorily (wajib) and three as recommended (mustahabb: encouraged, not required). The first is standing without leaning on anything; then standing while leaning; then sitting without leaning; then sitting while leaning.
passages.salah_seven_states.p02: Keeping to the order of these four is obligatory: if someone capable of one of them prays in a lower one, their prayer is invalid.
passages.salah_seven_states.p03: The three that are recommended are these: someone unable to manage the positions mentioned prays on their right side, then on their left side, then on their back. If they depart from this order among the three, their prayer is not invalidated.
passages.salah_seven_states.p04: The leaning that invalidates the prayer of someone able to do without it is leaning on a support such that the person would fall if it gave way. If they would not fall, the leaning is disliked (makruh).
passages.salah_seven_states.p05: As for voluntary prayers, someone able to stand may pray them sitting, and they receive half the reward of someone who stands. One may also begin sitting and then stand, or begin standing and then sit, unless one began intending to pray it standing, in which case sitting down afterwards is not allowed.
passages.qada_missed_prayers.p01: Prayers that one owes must be made up, and neglecting them is not permissible. Someone who makes up five days' worth [of prayers] every day is not neglectful.
passages.qada_missed_prayers.p02: They are made up in the form in which they were missed: a prayer missed while resident is made up as a resident's [full] prayer, and one missed while travelling is made up as a traveller's [shortened] prayer, whether one is resident or travelling at the time of making it up.
passages.qada_missed_prayers.p03: Keeping the order between the two current prayers [that share a time, such as Zuhr and 'Asr], and between a small number of missed prayers and the current one, is obligatory as long as one remembers. A small number means four prayers or fewer.
passages.qada_missed_prayers.p04: Someone who owes four prayers or fewer prays them before the current prayer, even if its time runs out. Making up prayers is allowed at any time.
passages.qada_missed_prayers.p05: Someone who owes make-up prayers does not pray voluntary prayers, nor the Duha (mid-morning) prayer, nor the night prayers of Ramadan. Nothing is permitted to them except shaf' and witr (the even and odd night prayers), [the two rak'ahs of] Fajr, the two 'Eid prayers, the eclipse prayer and the prayer for rain.
passages.qada_missed_prayers.p06: People who owe make-up prayers may pray them together in congregation if the prayers they owe are the same.
passages.qada_missed_prayers.p07: Someone who has forgotten how many prayers they owe prays enough to leave no doubt.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p01: The prostration of forgetfulness (sujud al-sahw: two extra prostrations that repair certain mistakes) is a sunnah (a practice established by the Prophet ﷺ). For something left out, one makes two prostrations before the closing salam, after completing the two tashahhuds, and then recites another tashahhud after them. For something added, one makes two prostrations after the salam, recites the tashahhud after them, and gives another salam.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p02: Someone who both left something out and added something prostrates before the salam.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p03: Someone who forgets the pre-salam prostration (qabli) until after giving the salam makes it if only a short time has passed. If much time has gone by, or they have left the mosque, the prostration lapses, and the prayer becomes invalid along with it if it was owed for three or more sunnahs; otherwise the prayer is not invalid.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p04: Someone who forgets the post-salam prostration (ba'di) makes it whenever they remember, even a year later.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p05: Someone who omits an obligatory act (fard) cannot make up for it with the prostration. Someone who omits meritorious acts (fada'il) owes no prostration.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p06: The pre-salam prostration is only owed for leaving out two or more sunnahs. A single sunnah needs no prostration, except quiet and loud recitation: someone who recites quietly where loud recitation is due prostrates before the salam, and someone who recites aloud where quiet recitation is due prostrates after the salam.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p07: Forgetful speech calls for a prostration after the salam. Forgetfully giving the salam after two rak'ahs (cycles of prayer) also calls for prostration after the salam. Adding one or two rak'ahs to the prayer calls for prostration after the salam; but adding as many rak'ahs as the prayer itself contains invalidates it.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p08: Someone unsure whether they have completed their prayer does what they are unsure about; doubt over whether something was left out counts as if it were certainly left out. So someone unsure whether they did a rak'ah or a prostration does it, then prostrates after the salam. Where the doubt is about the salam, they give it if only a short time has passed, owing no prostration; if much time has gone by, the prayer is invalid.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p09: A person troubled by obsessive doubts (muwaswis) should put the doubts out of their heart and not redo what they are unsure about, but they do prostrate after the salam, whether their doubt was about adding or leaving out.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p10: Someone who says the qunut aloud owes no prostration, though doing so deliberately is disliked. Someone who adds a surah in the last two rak'ahs owes no prostration.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p11: Someone who hears Muhammad ﷺ mentioned while praying, and invokes blessings on him, owes nothing, whether they did it forgetfully or deliberately, standing or sitting.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p12: Someone who recites two or more surahs in one rak'ah, moves from one surah to another, or bows before finishing the surah owes nothing for any of this. Someone who gestures with their hand or head during the prayer owes nothing.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p13: Someone who repeats the Fatihah forgetfully makes the prostration after the salam; if done on purpose, the evident ruling is that the repetition invalidates the prayer.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p14: Someone who remembers the surah after they have already bent down for bowing should not return to it. Someone who remembers [a mistake in] quiet or loud recitation before bowing repeats the recitation: if it was in the surah alone, they repeat it and owe no prostration; if it was in the Fatihah, they repeat it and make the post-salam prostration. If bowing has made it too late, they prostrate before the salam for omitting loud recitation, and after the salam for omitting quiet recitation, whether it was in the Fatihah or in the surah alone.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p15: Laughing in prayer invalidates it, whether forgetful or deliberate. Only a heedless person who is toying [with the prayer] laughs in it.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p16: When the believer stands to pray, their heart turns away from everything other than Allah, glorified is He, and leaves behind this world and all it holds, until their heart is fully present with the majesty and greatness of Allah, glorified is He; their heart trembles and their soul is filled with dread before the awe of Allah, whose majesty is exalted. Such is the prayer of the God-fearing (muttaqin).
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p17: Smiling carries no penalty. Weeping out of humility in prayer is excused. Someone who listens briefly to a person speaking owes nothing.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p18: Someone who rises after two rak'ahs without sitting [for the middle tashahhud]: if they remember before their hands and knees leave the ground, they return to sitting and owe no prostration. If they have left the ground, they carry on without returning and prostrate before the salam. If they return after leaving the ground and standing up, whether forgetfully or deliberately, their prayer is valid and they prostrate after the salam.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p19: Someone who blows [audibly] in their prayer out of forgetfulness makes the post-salam prostration; if done on purpose, their prayer is invalid.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p20: Someone who sneezes in prayer should not busy themselves with praising Allah, nor reply to someone who says "Yarhamuk Allah" (may Allah have mercy on you) to them, nor say it to someone else who sneezes. If they do praise Allah, they owe nothing.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p21: Someone who yawns in prayer covers their mouth. They should not spit except into their clothing, and without producing any [audible] letters.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p22: Someone who doubts whether they have lost their wudu or have impurity on them, thinks about it briefly during the prayer and then becomes sure they are pure, owes nothing.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p23: Turning [the head] in prayer out of forgetfulness carries no penalty; doing it deliberately is disliked. If one turns one's back to the qiblah, the prayer is broken off.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p24: Someone who prays wearing silk or gold [as a man], commits theft while praying, or gazes at something unlawful is sinning, but their prayer is valid.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p25: Someone who makes a mistake in recitation by saying a word from outside the Qur'an makes the post-salam prostration. If the mistaken word does belong to the Qur'an, they owe no prostration, unless it changes the wording [of the verse] or spoils the meaning, in which case they prostrate after the salam.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p26: Someone who dozes during the prayer owes no prostration; if the sleep becomes deep, they repeat both the prayer and the wudu.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p27: The groaning of a sick person is excused, and so is clearing the throat out of need. Clearing the throat to make someone understand something is objectionable, though it does not invalidate the prayer.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p28: If someone calls a person who is praying and they answer by saying "Subhan Allah", that is disliked, but their prayer is valid.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p29: Someone who gets stuck in their recitation, with no one prompting them, skips that verse and carries on with the next; if even that is not possible, they bow. They should not look at a mushaf in front of them, except for the Fatihah, which must be completed, whether from a mushaf or by other means. If they leave out one verse of it, they prostrate before the salam; if they leave out more, the prayer is invalid.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p30: Someone who prompts anyone other than their own imam invalidates their prayer. One should not prompt one's imam unless he is waiting to be prompted or [his mistake] spoils the meaning.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p31: Someone whose thoughts drift briefly to worldly matters loses some of the reward, but the prayer is not invalid.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p32: Someone who pushes back a person walking in front of them, or puts the side of their forehead down in prostration, or on one or two folds of their turban, owes nothing. Nothing is owed for vomiting or reflux (qals: fluid rising from the stomach) that one cannot hold back during the prayer.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p33: The imam carries the follower's (ma'mum's) forgetfulness, unless it involves leaving out an obligatory act.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p34: If a follower, in a rak'ah other than the first, is distracted, dozes, or is crowded out so that they miss the bowing: if they hope to reach the imam before he lifts his head from the second prostration, they bow and catch up with him. If they have no such hope, they leave the bowing, follow their imam, and make up a rak'ah in its place after the imam's salam.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p35: If they miss the prostration through distraction, crowding or dozing until the imam has stood for the next rak'ah, they prostrate if they hope to reach the imam before he bows; otherwise they leave it, follow the imam, and make up another rak'ah as well. Whenever a rak'ah is made up [in this way], no prostration of forgetfulness is owed, unless they were unsure about the bowing or prostration.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p36: Someone approached by a scorpion or a snake who kills it owes nothing, unless doing so takes long or they turn their back to the qiblah, in which case they break off [the prayer].
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p37: Someone unsure whether they are in the witr (the single closing night prayer) or in the second rak'ah of the shaf' (the two-rak'ah prayer before it) treats it as the second rak'ah of the shaf', makes the post-salam prostration, then prays the witr.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p38: Someone who speaks forgetfully between shaf' and witr owes nothing; if they did so deliberately, it is disliked, but they still owe nothing.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p39: A latecomer (masbuq) who catches less than a full rak'ah with the imam does not make either the pre-salam or the post-salam prostration with him; if they do, their prayer is invalid. If they catch a full rak'ah or more, they make the pre-salam prostration with him, and delay the post-salam one until they finish their own prayer, making it after their own salam. If they deliberately make [the post-salam one] with the imam, their prayer is invalid; if they did so forgetfully, they prostrate after the salam.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p40: If the latecomer makes a mistake after the imam's salam, they are like someone praying alone. If a latecomer owes a post-salam prostration because of the imam and a pre-salam prostration because of their own mistake, the pre-salam prostration is enough.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p41: Someone who forgets to bow and remembers during the prostration goes back to standing. It is recommended for them to go over part of the recitation again; then they bow, and they prostrate after the salam.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p42: Someone who forgets one prostration and remembers after standing up goes back to sitting and makes the prostration, unless they had already sat before standing, in which case they do not repeat the sitting.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p43: Someone who forgets both prostrations drops straight into prostration without sitting first. In each of these cases, they prostrate after the salam.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p44: If they remember the missed prostration only after raising their head from the bowing of the following rak'ah, they carry on with their prayer and do not go back. They cancel the rak'ah in which the mistake happened and add a rak'ah in its place, building on [what is valid]. They prostrate before the salam if [the cancelled rak'ah] was among the first two and they remembered after completing [the bowing of] the third. The prostration comes after the salam when that rak'ah was not among the first two, or was among them but they remembered before completing the third, since in that case neither the surah nor the sitting has been missed.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p45: Someone who gives the salam while unsure whether their prayer is complete invalidates their prayer.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p46: Forgetfulness in a make-up prayer is treated like forgetfulness in a prayer prayed on time (ada').
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p47: Forgetfulness in a voluntary prayer (nafilah) is treated like forgetfulness in an obligatory one, except in six matters: the Fatihah; the surah; quiet recitation; loud recitation; adding a rak'ah; and leaving out some of the pillars (arkan: essential acts) through forgetfulness, when a long time has passed.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p48: So someone who forgets the Fatihah in a voluntary prayer and remembers after bowing carries on and prostrates before the salam. In an obligatory prayer, by contrast, they cancel that rak'ah, add another and carry on, and their prostration follows what we described for someone who left out a prostration.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p49: Someone who forgets the surah, or the loud or quiet recitation, in a voluntary prayer and remembers after bowing carries on and owes no prostration, unlike in an obligatory prayer.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p50: Someone who stands up for a third rak'ah in a voluntary prayer: if they remember before completing the bowing, they go back and make the post-salam prostration. If they have completed [the bowing of] the third, they carry on, add a fourth, and prostrate before the salam. In an obligatory prayer, by contrast, they go back whenever they remember and prostrate after the salam.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p51: Someone who forgets a pillar of a voluntary prayer, such as bowing or prostration, and only remembers after the salam once a long time has passed, owes no repetition of it; unlike an obligatory prayer, which must be repeated no matter how much time has passed.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p52: Someone who deliberately breaks off a voluntary prayer, or deliberately leaves out a rak'ah or a prostration from it, must repeat it, no matter how much time has passed.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p53: Someone who sighs during their prayer owes nothing, unless they utter [actual] letters.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p54: If the imam forgets, by leaving something out or adding something, the follower says "Subhan Allah" to alert him.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p55: If your imam stands up after two rak'ahs [without sitting], say "Subhan Allah" to him; but if he has already risen off the ground, follow him.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p56: If he sits down in the first rak'ah or the third, stand and do not join him in sitting.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p57: If he makes one prostration and leaves out the second, say "Subhan Allah" to him and do not rise with him, unless you are afraid he will complete the bowing [of the next rak'ah], in which case follow him; and from then on do not sit with him, whether in the second rak'ah or the fourth. When he gives the salam, add another rak'ah in place of the one you cancelled, building on [what is valid], and make the pre-salam prostration. If there are several of you, it is better for you to put one person forward to lead you in completing the prayer.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p58: Should the imam add a third prostration, say "Subhan Allah" to him and do not join him in it.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p59: Should the imam rise for a fifth rak'ah, those who are certain it is needed, or who are unsure, follow him; those who are certain it is extra stay seated. If someone in the first group sits, or someone in the second group stands, their prayer is invalid.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.p60: If the imam gives the salam before the prayer is complete, those behind him say "Subhan Allah". If he accepts what they say, he completes the prayer and makes the post-salam prostration. Should he doubt their report, he asks two upright, trustworthy people ('adl), and the two may speak in order to answer him. If he is certain the prayer is complete, he acts on his certainty and disregards the two, unless the people behind him are many; then he sets aside his certainty and goes by what they say.

obligations_of_the_mukallaf.p07: The items in square brackets are missing from the OpenITI Arabic and are restored from the Cairo (Subayh) edition.

“Making a living out of religion”: the vowelled Subayh edition reads «بِالدِّين» (bi-l-din, “by means of religion”), that is, taking people's money on the strength of one's religious standing. The Tayba and Saidy translations read it the same way. Aisha Bewley's translation reads bi-l-dayn (“by means of a debt”), that is, profiting from a loan. This translation follows bi-l-din.
wudu_faraid_sunan.p06: The printed Arabic (both the OpenITI text and the Subayh edition) reads «ويجب تخليل أصابع الرجلين», “it is obligatory to work water between the toes”. This translation follows the relied-upon (mashhur) Maliki position: working water between the fingers is obligatory, and between the toes recommended (mandub). See Khalil, al-Mukhtasar, section on wudu: «بتخليل أصابعه» for the hands and «وندب تخليل أصابعهما» for the feet.
wudu_nullifiers.p02: In the relied-upon Maliki position, a kiss on the mouth breaks wudu whether or not pleasure was intended or felt; other touching breaks it only when pleasure is intended or felt (Khalil, al-Mukhtasar: «إلا القبلة بفم مطلقا»).
acts_requiring_wudu.p04: Commentators restrict this statement. Al-Kashnawi (Ashal al-Madarik sharh Irshad al-Salik, vol. 1, p. 100), commenting on the commentary on al-Akhdari Hidayat al-Muta'abbid al-Salik, explains it as referring to someone who leaves out wudu while denying that it is obligatory, or out of contempt and disregard for Allah's command. Someone who does it out of laziness, ignorance, forgetfulness or necessity, while believing that purification is obligatory, is not a disbeliever. He is a sinner who must repent, and the prayer is invalid and must be repeated.
hayd_menstruation.p03: This is the Maliki position (compare Khalil, al-Mukhtasar: «وللحامل بعد ثلاثة أشهر النصف ونحوه، وفي ستة فأكثر عشرون يوما ونحوها»). The commentators explain “or thereabouts” in different ways. Al-Hattab (Mawahib al-Jalil) reports “up to twenty days” for the first case, and either “up to twenty-five” or “up to thirty” for the second. They also discuss bleeding before the third month. A woman should ask a qualified scholar about her own case.
sahw_forgetfulness.p07: Khalil's Mukhtasar states this rule as adding four rak'ahs, or two in a two-rak'ah prayer («وبزيادة أربع كركعتين في الثنائية»). Ask a teacher how this applies to Maghrib.
